plans.note: Section 21 is the operative cap: 21.1 mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; 21.2 consequential-damages exclusion with direct-damage carve-back; 21.3 defines Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnity, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, IP infringement); 21.4 savings language. Check mutuality, cap size against annual spend (sec-2.1 USD 2M/yr) and whether carve-outs are uncapped.

No Section 20 appears in the outline even though sec-9.3 cross-references 'the remedies required by Section 20.5' and sec-21.3 and sec-30.5 assume indemnification obligations and indemnified parties exist. Verify whether an indemnity article was dropped; if truly absent, treat as missing and note the dangling cross-reference.

sec-12.4-2 imposes a 24-month, all-territory non-compete on Customer — squarely prohibited by the playbook and inconsistent with sec-12.3, which recites that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. Flag sec-12.4-2 and cite the sec-12.3 conflict.

sec-7.2 (first of the two 7.2s) requires Customer to disclose and match any better offer before engaging another provider — a de facto right of first refusal restricting our freedom to source elsewhere. sec-12.3 is the protective free-dealing clause that contradicts it; do not double-flag with MFN unless both limbs are independently breached.

sec-7.2 is an MFN running against us (we must disclose and match third-party offers for Vendor's benefit); sec-12.3 states no most-favoured-customer commitment was made. Direction is wrong — MFN must run in our favour or be deleted.

sec-12.4 (first) is a one-way 24-month no-hire on Customer covering any Vendor employee 'regardless of how the employee applies' — no general-advertising carve-out and hire (not just solicit) is barred. sec-12.3 preserves general recruitment hiring and conflicts.

Section 9 contains only cause-based termination (breach, insolvency, security/SLA/law/IP) plus Order-Form-level rights in sec-6.2 and sec-27.3; there is no Section 9.4 and no convenience right, and sec-2.1 expressly denies reduction or termination rights. Confirm no convenience clause elsewhere before treating as missing.

sec-8.2 gives 12-month auto-renewal with only 30 days' non-renewal notice from Customer plus a 60-day Vendor reminder and deadline extension if missed; sec-8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Assess against the preferred notice window; the reminder mechanic and uplift cap are favourable to us.

Direct conflict: sec-28.1 imposes Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction (outside the accepted list), while sec-28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts. sec-28.3 is a pre-suit executive escalation that preserves urgent relief. Resolve to an accepted law/venue pairing.

sec-24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent; sec-24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and change of control; sec-24.3 residual consent standard; sec-24.4 bars Vendor from terminating or repricing on our change of control. sec-13.3 lets us transfer licence rights consistently. Likely compliant — confirm no hidden Vendor exit right.

sec-14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP (good), but sec-14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for Customer with only a revocable, non-transferable term licence — wrong direction on work we pay for. Read with sec-1.4, sec-14.3 (Vendor Technology plus sec-13.2 perpetual licence) and sec-15.1 (no training/model use).

sec-13.1 covers Affiliates and contractors; sec-13.2 grants a perpetual, irrevocable, paid-up licence for delivered/embedded Vendor Technology; sec-13.3 limits revocation to uncured material breach after notice. The revocability problem sits in sec-14.2's Deliverable licence — address there to avoid double-flagging the same term.

sec-22.1 limits Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor; sec-22.2 puts costs on Vendor absent >5% underpayment and bars system/data access; sec-22.3 protects findings. Likely compliant; sec-23 (records/assurance) has no text shown — check for a broader inspection right.

No liquidated-damages or penalty clause payable by Customer appears; sec-1.5 references service credits only in the Fees exclusion and sec-7.3 bars interest on amounts not due. The take-or-pay in sec-2.1 is economically penal but is addressed under MINCOMMIT — do not double-flag.

sec-19.1–19.3 give services, conformity, malicious-code and legal-compliance warranties (90 days post-delivery/acceptance for Deliverables; term-long for hosted Services); sec-19.4 provides repair/re-perform then terminate-and-refund, expressly non-exclusive for key claims; sec-19.5 is a balanced disclaimer. Likely compliant.

sec-18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M for the term plus one year; sec-18.2 covers insurer quality, certificates, cancellation notice and non-limitation of liability. Check limits against data sensitivity but the clause is present.

sec-2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per year, three-year take-or-pay 'without reduction or termination rights' — a walk-away term under the playbook and directly contradicted by sec-12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement. Needs an exit, carry-forward or shortfall-only remedy.

sec-10.1 assumes 'any agreed transition period' and sec-10.2 covers Deliverable delivery and refunds, but no clause obliges Vendor to provide exit assistance or to return/export Customer Data in a usable format; sec-16.5 cross-references a Section 11 on Customer Data that does not appear in the outline. Verify the missing Section 11 before concluding.
